messages.subject: rstan stops working
parts:
I've been using rstan 2.7.0 on a seemingly up-to-date R 3.2.2, and it just stopped working.  It's certainly possible I did an update over the past few days when I wasn't using Stan and corrupted something.  As the problem seemed to involve Rcpp (and a simple Rcpp test seemed to fail), I removed and reinstalled both Rcpp and rstan.  I checked, and RcppEigen was built under 3.2.1, so I removed and reinstalled it, too.

I've attached a trace of the problem while executing stan_demo(318) from a fresh start.  I did search on dump_factory.hpp but found nothing.  I searched on other people's problems with rstan installations and also found nothing.  I did not go so far as to reinstall R.

I was using rstan under org-mode when it happened (and I may have updated org-mode recently, too), but the problem obviously exists in RStudio.

Any ideas?  Is there any more information that might help?  Here is sessionInfo():

> sessionInfo()

other attached packages:

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
[1] tools_3.2.2  stats4_3.2.2

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: rstan stops working
parts:
On Thursday, September 17, 2015 at 5:23:35 PM UTC-4, Bill Harris wrote:
Any ideas?  Is there any more information that might help?  Here is sessionInfo():

[Workspace loaded from Z:/.RData]

This often messes things up, particularly if you have a stanfit object from an older version of rstan in .RData. You could delete.RData or start R with the --no-restore-data flag. If that isn't the source of the problem, make sure your StanHeaders is compatible with your rstan. At the moment, there is a new StanHeaders on CRAN but not a new rstan for a day or two.

Ben

https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/commit/f812cb5c379ea16e664707a872cb6a2fb5141de9

so when that was merged, rstan on GitHub would no longer work with StanHeaders from CRAN. But if you have rstan from CRAN and it is not being superceded by an rstan from GitHub, then I don't understand why this error would occur.

CmdStan is fine. You can read the .csv files it generates into R with stan_read_csv().

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: rstan stops working
parts:
On Friday, September 18, 2015 at 4:59:23 PM UTC-4, Bill Harris wrote:
I see the benefit of having lots of demos, but does it make any sense to unrelease or otherwise mark those that you don't expect to work until they eventually do?  Given the history of BDA, it's not surprising that eight_schools is among those that work.

That would make sense, but it is not the way we do it. Basically, the example-models are supposed to demonstrate how things could be done (often suboptimally) in the Stan language and almost all of them do parse correctly. Moreover, a human could probably get the vast majority of them to run manually after figuring out which data goes with which example. So, they are not going to disappear just because rstan can't run them automatically.

Ben
